---
title: "McEagle-300, AeroBuildup"
---

The McEagle — Norm Poff's Styrofoam-tray glider plan, published by the
Aerospace Education Services Project at Oklahoma State University — scaled to a
300 mm wingspan and cut from foam sheet weighing 27 g per A3, run through
`AeroBuildup`.

- **`AeroBuildup` on 3D geometry**, with NeuralFoil section data.
- **Flat foam section**, 5.7% thick, approximated as a NACA 0006.
- **Geometry traced off the plan sheet**, scaled 1.380× from its printed 217 mm
  span; only the tail incidence and the sheet thickness are assumed.
- **The fuselage plate is a body**, 10 mm wide over the traced depth profile,
  carrying force as well as mass. Its mass comes from the traced plan area, not
  from the body's volume — a super-ellipse under-fills the rectangular slab.
- **Ballast is not a constant here.** The plan trims the glider by taping a dime
  to the fuselage; the structure alone sits behind its own neutral point, so
  where the ballast goes is a question for an entry.
- **Fixed speed per run**, since Re is ~2–4 × 10⁴ here.

## The model

`_model.py` says what the aircraft is; `_analysis.py` says how this chapter
measures it. Both are read straight off disk rather than copied, so these
listings cannot drift from what the entries actually run.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import pathlib

for _f in ["_model.py", "_analysis.py"]:
    code = pathlib.Path(f"chapters/02-mceagle-300/{_f}").read_text()
    print('::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}')
    print(f"## `{_f}`\n")
    print("```python")
    print(code.strip())
    print("```")
    print(":::")
    print()
```
